newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen little moved by Deng death.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen little moved by Deng death.

text.p: Tokyo share prices are unlikely to be greatly affected by news that China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping has died, brokers said on Thursday.
"I don't think there will be an impact on stocks, and foreign exchange looks unaffected," said Yasuo Ueki, a general manager at Nikko Securities. "He had no political influence."

Brokers said Tokyo share investors were paying more attention to matters such as the direction of prices of multinational blue-chip firms, which have been supporting the market recently but which on Wednesday fell prey to some profit-taking.
"The Tokyo stock market will probably pay little attention," said Paul Migliorato, a senior salesman at Jardine Fleming Securities.

"I think they are more concerned with the fate of Sony than with that of Deng Xiaoping. What matters most to investors is that blue chips have supported the market so far, and that will be the market focus," Migliorato said.
Deng died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection. The announcement of his death was made by the Communist Party.

"Compared to two or three years ago, the political climate in China is much more stable now, and the power has already shifted from Deng to the other leaders," said Kazuto Uchida, chief strategist at Tokyo-Mitsubishi Securities.
"Judging from the fact that there was little reaction to the news in overseas markets, I don't see much action coming from stock and foreign exchange markets here either," he said.
He added that most of the shock of Deng's death had already been absorbed in the markets because news of his deteriorating health had already spread earlier this week.
"Brokers may be inclined to stay on the sidelines until the Hong Kong market opens and see its reaction to Deng's death," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.

But another broker said: "The death of China's senior leader is unlikely to have a significant impact on the Tokyo market. Participants will rather focus on the report of possible injection of government funds to solve the bad loan problem."
Market sources predicted the Nikkei 225 would trade in a range between 18,400 and 18,900.
